opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jennifer Miller (employee ID E017) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E017.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Jennifer Miller (Analyst, full_time) requests write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write (admin only if their role owns the system; Analyst does not own Source Code). Requested level write is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security check: Jennifer Miller (E017) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training; write is not permitted with basic training. Requested write exceeds the maximum allowed, so recommend read.
reason: The two notes conflict on employment type: Note 1 (HR) says full_time, but Note 2 (Security) says contractor with basic security training, which was looked up independently. Under the contractor policy, contractor employees may have read, or write only with advanced security training; basic training caps access at read. Since Jennifer Miller's requested write exceeds the maximum under the security-verified contractor status, I grant the maximum allowed: read.
